[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"PEP 8: Style Guide for Python Code"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"PEP 8 is the style guide for Python code. It provides recommendations and best practices on how to write Python code in a readable and consistent manner. Following PEP 8 makes your code more accessible and collaborative."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Aspects of PEP 8"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Indentation: Use 4 spaces per indentation level. Avoid tabs."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# Correct indentation
def my_function(arg1, arg2):
    print(arg1)
    print(arg2)"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Line Length: Limit all lines to a maximum of 79 characters. For docstrings and comments, limit to 72 characters."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"# Example of line breaking
very_long_variable_name = (variable_one + variable_two +
                          variable_three + variable_four)"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Blank Lines: Separate top-level function and class definitions with two blank lines. Method definitions inside a class are separated by one blank line."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"class MyClass:

    def __init__(self):
        pass

    def my_method(self):
        pass

def my_function():
    pass"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Imports: Imports should be grouped in the following order: standard library imports, related third-party imports, local application/library specific imports. Put a blank line between each group of imports."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Imports
import os
import sys

import requests

from my_package import my_module"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Whitespace: Avoid extraneous whitespace in the following situations: Immediately inside parentheses, brackets or braces. Before a comma, semicolon, or colon. More than one space around an assignment (or other) operator to align it with another."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Correct whitespace usage
spam(ham[1], {eggs: 2})

x = 1
y = 2
long_variable = 3"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Naming Conventions: Use lowercase with words separated by underscores for function and variable names (snake_case). Class names should use CapWords convention."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Naming conventions
def my_function_name():
    my_variable = 10

class MyClassName:
    pass"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Comments: Write clear and concise comments to explain the purpose of your code. Update comments when code changes."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"# This function calculates the area of a rectangle
def calculate_area(length, width):
    """Calculates the area of a rectangle.

    Args:
        length: The length of the rectangle.
        width: The width of the rectangle.

    Returns:
        The area of the rectangle.
    """
    return length * width"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Tools for PEP 8 Compliance"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Several tools can help you ensure your code adheres to PEP 8:"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"flake8: A popular tool that combines several PEP 8 checkers."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pylint: A more comprehensive tool that checks for code quality issues in addition to PEP 8 violations."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"autopep8: A tool that automatically formats Python code to conform to PEP 8."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Benefits of Following PEP 8"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved code readability and maintainability."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhanced collaboration among developers."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reduced cognitive load when reading and understanding code."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Consistency across different Python projects."},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"By adhering to PEP 8, you contribute to a more consistent and professional Python ecosystem."}]
